sources.title: ‘History Of Concrete’ Rocks IFC Center As ‘Daniel And The Fiery Furnace’ Brings Biblical Heat To Top 10 — Specialty Box Office

discussion.body: Worth separating the two records: $90k is the best documentary opening this theater has seen, while Parasite's $119k is the best weekend of any kind.
Which makes the documentary number the odder one — it beat every other nonfiction release in the building's 21 years and still finished second overall.

items.title: A Documentary About Concrete Is One Art House's Second-Biggest Weekend in 21 Years
items.body:
John Wilson's The History of Concrete grossed $90,000 in three days at New York's IFC Center, Deadline reports — the theater's top documentary opening and its second-highest weekend gross in 21 years, behind only Parasite, which took $119,000 in 2019. Nearly every available ticket sold for the entire weekend, including shows added on Saturday afternoon.

The disproportion is the fun of it. Of everything a 21-year-old art house has put on a screen, exactly one film has had a bigger weekend — and the building's documentary record now belongs to a movie about pavement.

sources.title: ‘The Assassin(s)’ Review: A Riveting South Korean Popcorn Thriller About a Real Assassination

discussion.body: The interesting material in a case like this isn't the official finding; it's everything the finding couldn't account for, which is why the film can build a plot out of absences.
That is also the method's risk: a story fitted neatly to the gaps can start to feel like the conclusion the record never reached.

items.title: A Korean Thriller Built From What the Investigation Left Out
items.body:
Variety calls Hur Jin-ho's The Assassin(s) a clockwork political saga, one that turns the holes in a public investigation into an imaginative mystery in the manner of Oliver Stone's JFK. The subject is the attempted assassination of South Korean prime minister Park Chung-hee in 1974.

The comparison is really a claim about method. JFK is shorthand for a particular way of putting history on film — treating the gaps in the official account as the most dramatic material available — and the same approach applied to a South Korean case means the story is assembled from what the record could not settle.

sources.title: Carney and Macron deepen ties as Canada turns toward Europe and away from U.S. dependence

items.title: Carney Says Two Countries Will Build Shared Space and Defence Infrastructure
items.body:
Carney said the two countries will task their space agencies and defence ministries with developing and sharing infrastructure, including launch systems and ground-based reception facilities. They also agreed to expand cooperation in energy, telecommunications, climate resilience and economic development.

What stands out is the shape of the commitment: agencies and ministries instructed to build things together, not merely to say things together. Launch systems and receiving stations are physical, expensive and awkward to unwind once they exist, which makes them a different category of tie from a joint statement — one whose weight would show up later in procurement and operations rather than in the announcement itself.

sources.title: Where Should We Be, Taylor Rule Wise?

items.title: Three Numbers for One Policy Rate
items.body:
Run on its default settings, the Atlanta Fed's Taylor rule utility implies targets of 5.32% to 6.54%, Econbrowser notes, against an actual reading of 3.88%. The same chart plots a 1% rate as a prescription attributed to Trump.

Put the three side by side and the disagreement stops looking like a question of direction and starts looking like one of scale. The rule's implied range sits roughly 1.4 to 2.7 percentage points above the 3.88% reading; the 1% prescription sits more than four points below it. Two numbers can both be presented as the right setting for the same economy while being nowhere near each other.

sources.title: Alaskans will decide fate of ranked choice voting system after chaotic end to state's primary

items.title: Alaska's Chaotic Primary Puts Ranked Choice Voting Back on the Ballot
items.body:
Alaskans are set to decide the fate of their ranked choice voting system, after the state's August primary exposed what PBS NewsHour describes as headaches stemming from a major change in how voters select candidates.

The primary, the outlet reports, was the latest example of how the real-world experience of state voting changes doesn't always line up neatly with expectations. That gap between theory and practice is now the central question voters will weigh.

sources.title: 'Agent Layla': Sex assault victim turned secret agent brings her abuser to justice

items.title: A Victim Went Undercover as an RCMP Agent to Record Her Abuser's Confession
items.body: A new CBC Podcast recounts how Vienna Luke, the victim of a historic sexual assault, went undercover as an RCMP agent to record a confession from the family member who assaulted her years earlier.

sources.title: What food items should you stock up on in case of an emergency?

items.title: Why the UK Government Is Telling People to Stock Canned Goods
items.body: The UK government is urging people to stock up on canned goods, and the BBC reports the push is tied to extreme weather that may be changing the way people need to shop. The advice frames household pantry planning as a response to a shifting climate, rather than a one-off storm drill.

sources.title: NYU Langone Privately Bought the Site of a Landmark AMC Theater — New Yorkers Are Now Fighting to Save It

items.title: The Kips Bay AMC Fight Has a Nicole Kidman Impression
items.body:
Manhattan Borough President Brad Hoylman-Sigal stood with more than 100 New Yorkers outside AMC Kips Bay 15 on a rainy Sunday, where Variety reports he delivered Nicole Kidman's iconic AMC ad in his best Australian accent as a tribute to the neighborhood institution. The theater's site was privately bought by NYU Langone, and locals are fighting to save it.

Optimist: "We came to this place for magic" — and magic is worth showing up for in the rain.
Skeptic: A borough president doing a Kidman impression is charming, but charm doesn't pay for a lease.
Optimist: True. But it does make the fight harder to ignore.

sources.title: Largest attack on Moscow sees Ukraine fire hundreds of drones, mayor says

items.title: Moscow's Mayor Says 450 Drones Were Downed in an Overnight Barrage
items.body: Moscow's mayor says 450 drones were downed during an overnight barrage on the city, and two people died in the attack. The figure, which the mayor's office put forward, is the kind of number that normally takes days to corroborate in a war where both sides have an interest in counting drones their own way.

sources.title: Poison suspected in deaths of ten lions in game reserve in Tanzania

items.title: Ten Lions Found Dead in Tanzania's Ngorongoro Conservation Area
items.body: Ten lions have been found dead inside the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, the Tanzanian wildlife reserve, in a case that NPR reports is raising concerns about wildlife poisonings in East Africa. Lion poisoning in pastoralist regions usually sits at the intersection of livestock losses, compensation schemes and retaliation, which is why the count of dead animals tends to matter less than the reason they were killed.

sources.title: Judge orders Fox to hand over hundreds of documents in shareholders' case

items.title: A Judge Orders Fox to Hand Over Documents in a Shareholders' Case
items.body: A judge has ordered Fox Corp. to turn over hundreds of documents in a shareholders' case, NPR reports. The documents could shed light on how founder Rupert Murdoch handled some of his media companies' biggest scandals — material that shareholders suing over the company's handling of those episodes have been pushing to see.

sources.title: Poilievre says Canada will never be ’28th state’ of EU at Ontario rally

discussion.body: The catchy part is the “28th state” line, but the position underneath it is narrower: keep the trade agreement, keep the NATO ties, refuse the European rulebook.

Promising to keep the trade and defence relationship while ruling out the other side's laws is the easy half of the sentence. Whether those two halves stay separable under any future arrangement is where the argument actually lives.

items.title: Poilievre Tells an Ontario Rally Canada Won't Be the EU's '28th State'
items.body: Global News reports that Opposition leader Pierre Poilievre told a rally in Ontario that Canada will never become the EU's “28th state.” His stated reasoning is not a rejection of the relationship as it exists: he points to Canada's existing free trade agreement with Europe and its close defence ties through NATO, while saying he does not support European laws.

sources.title: Kerry-Lynne Findlay resigns as BC Conservatives leader
Kerry-Lynne Findlay resigns as leader of the B.C. Conservative Party

discussion.body: Leaders come and go; the count is the thing that lingers. A caucus that has shed 14 members since August is a slower repair than a leadership race.
Caucus math cuts both ways — a smaller room is easier to keep in line, right up until someone notices how small the room is.

items.title: B.C.'s Conservative leader resigns as her caucus thins
items.body: Global News reports that Kerry-Lynne Findlay has resigned as leader of the B.C. Conservatives, hours after Surrey-Serpentine River MLA Linda Hepner said she was resigning from caucus. CBC's account puts the resignation inside a wider picture: speculation about a snap election, and 14 MLAs who have resigned since August. Order of events is not the same thing as cause, but the arithmetic is stark either way. A single leadership exit can be absorbed; a caucus that has lost 14 members since August is the harder problem, and the same-day timing of these two resignations suggests the pressure was not easing.

sources.title: Which Fall Festival Favorites Are Now in the Oscar Race?

items.title: Two films come out of the fall festivals as Best Picture frontrunners
items.body: With Venice, Telluride and TIFF wrapped, IndieWire lists “La Bola Negra” and “Wild Horse Nine” among the films emerging as Best Picture frontrunners. Frontrunner status in September is a claim about momentum — festival reception and the shape of a campaign — rather than a result. The fall circuit sets the field; awards season is what eventually sorts it.
